evidence: I did not run anything, including the tests. This is a read-only review of the diff and the worktree.

F1 (Go declarations): the three Go regexes (goFunc, goType, goNames) now start with `^` and no `\s*`. An indented `var err error` or `const n = 1` inside a function body therefore yields no removed name.

F1: the shell regexes (shKey, shParen) keep `^\s*`, so indented shell functions are still read. declaredNames in engine/review/sweep.go:54-79 applies the same patterns to both removed and added lines, so the new rule is symmetric and creates no asymmetry between the two sides.

F1 tests: sweep_test.go adds cases for an indented Go func, a local var, a local const, a column-0 var that is still read, and an indented shell function that is still read. All of them match the new regexes.

F2 (polisher size check): ParsePolisherFindings still bounds the input at MaxReplyBytes and now delegates to checkPolisherShape. DecodePolisher calls checkPolisherShape directly, so an indented stored file over 1 MiB is no longer rejected on read.

F2: EncodePolisher refuses a data length over MaxStoredBytes (8 MiB) with ErrReplyTooLarge and returns nil. fsstore.go:223-228 reads with a limit of MaxStoredBytes+1 and rejects only a file over MaxStoredBytes. The two bounds are consistent, so any record that is stored reads back.

F2 tests: the near-limit test uses a reply under 1 MiB whose stored file is over 1 MiB and checks that it round-trips. The deep-nesting test (depth 5000) checks that the encoder refuses, returns nil data, and the error wraps ErrReplyTooLarge. Indentation grows quadratically with depth, so at depth 5000 the file passes 8 MiB (my arithmetic, not measured).
I found no change outside rolerecords.go, sweep.go, their tests and the CHANGELOG. I found no secrets, path, exec or net surface in the diff. Risk none is consistent with that.
